subject: Cognitive Science
title: Predictive Processing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Predictive Processing.

hook.text: Your brain doesn't wait for input. It generates a prediction of what's coming and checks it against reality.

buildup.text: Karl Friston's framework says the brain is a prediction machine, constantly running a model of the world.

discovery.text: When predictions match input, nothing happens. When they don't, a prediction error signal fires—and you notice.

twist.text: This means perception is mostly hallucination constrained by data. You see your expectations, corrected by senses.

climax.text: Anxiety may be a prediction error disorder—the brain constantly predicting threats that never arrive.

punchline.text: You perceive what you expect—and only notice when you're wrong.

quiz.question: What fires when perception doesn't match prediction?
